cards.a: Using VRFs without MPLS or MP-BGP: separate routing tables and interfaces provide L3 segmentation on a single router. It is cheap and simple, ideal for small multi-tenant or service-separation designs.

cards.q: What is the key difference between VRF-lite and MPLS L3VPN?
cards.a: VRF-lite uses no MPLS and no MP-BGP, has no label stack, scales to small size, and is single-site; MPLS L3VPN uses MPLS + MP-BGP, two-label forwarding, scales large, and spans the WAN.

cards.q: How does VRF-lite work across routers?
cards.a: Each router on the path defines a VRF per tenant, binds interfaces per VRF, uses per-VRF IGP or static routes, and every link end must map to the same VRF.

cards.q: What configurations create a VRF-lite VRF and bind an interface?
cards.a: ip vrf GUEST with an optional rd 65000:10, then ip vrf forwarding GUEST plus ip address on the interface, and address-family ipv4 vrf GUEST under router bgp for per-VRF BGP.

cards.q: What are the use cases for VRF-lite?
cards.a: Small sites with cheap isolation, separate guest/management tables, lab segmentation, and simplified enterprise-core designs. It suits single-site segmentation without a service provider.

cards.q: What are the limitations of VRF-lite?
cards.a: Manual scaling per hop, RD/RT are not global (local only), no WAN/MPLS transit, and per-device complexity. Beyond a few devices, MPLS VPNs scale better.
show ip vrf (and detail), show ip route vrf GUEST, show ip cef vrf GUEST, and ping vrf GUEST to test reachability inside the VRF.

cards.q: Routes don't appear in VRF-lite after configuration. What should you check?
cards.a: Confirm the link is assigned to the VRF (show ip vrf), verify both ends map the same VRF to the link, and check that the BGP address-family for the VRF is configured.

cards.q: How does VRF-lite compare on MPLS, MP-BGP, and labels?
cards.a: VRF-lite has no MPLS, no MP-BGP, and no label stack; this lack of labels is its scale limit, making L3VPN the scalable upgrade path.

cards.q: What is the role of RD in VRF-lite?
cards.a: The rd is optional and only locally relevant in VRF-lite; route targets are not used globally because MP-BGP is not involved.

cards.q: Match the quick review: MPLS, MP-BGP, isolation, scope, scale, RD/RT, WAN, upgrade.
cards.a: MPLS = none; MP-BGP = none; isolation = per-router; scope = single site; scale = small; RD/RT = local; WAN = no; upgrade = MPLS L3VPN.
